newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Consumer groups want EU action on car safety.
newsitem.headline: Consumer groups want EU action on car safety.

text.p: European consumer organisations urged the European Union on Monday to strengthen its car safety legislation to take account of new crash tests showing that some vehicles posed a risk to passengers and pedestrians.

"The results of crash tests published today show that many car manufacturers are still dragging their feet where safety is concerned," the European Consumers' Organisation (BEUC) and International Testing said in a statement.

They urged the EU to bring forward urgently rules to require cars to meet pedestrian-safety standards developed by the European Experimental Vehicle Committee (EEVC), saying none of the seven cars tested would have passed the EEVC's tests.
They said the European Commission had delayed a proposal in this area under pressure from the car industry about the costs involved.
Commission spokesman Jochen Kubosch said he was not familiar with the groups' claims and could not comment immediately.

The groups also urged the EU to strengthen two existing directives on protection of passengers in frontal and side impacts -- 96/79/EC and 96/27/EC -- which apply to new types of cars on October 1, 1998 and all new cars on October 2003.
